title: A positive-gap obstruction and a wider Jacobi construction
question: Do positive short-gap Jacobi corrections satisfy the four limiting quotient equations through R5? If not, does repartitioning the comparison into two wide factors admit a nonsingular solution while keeping both actual factor gaps positive? Verify the exact algebra, show a rational positive-rooted comparison, and identify the analytic assumptions needed to transfer the limiting construction to RH coefficient matching.

definitions.coefficient_domain: R0=1 and every relevant R_j is strictly positive

finite_witness.meaning: An illustrative exact comparison with a negative cross-junction offset and positive actual factor gaps; these parameters were not fitted to Riemann-xi coefficients.

exact_algebra: Wide R5 limiting solution and Jacobian
Exact positive-root isolation for the rational witness
conditional: Finite-n local existence requires the C1 convergence hypothesis stated in mathematics.md
not_established: An RH coefficient match at any specified n

references.title: Jonathan Holland, A new hyperbolicity wedge and a joint semicircle limit for Jensen polynomials of Riemann's xi-function, arXiv:2608.08682v1
references.scope: Source quotient coordinates and two-factor comparison conventions. This example checks the selected extension's algebra; it is not a validation of the paper's full analytic theorem.

references.title: Andrei Martinez-Finkelshtein, Rafael Morales and Daniel Perales, Real roots of hypergeometric polynomials via finite free convolution, arXiv:2309.10970v3
references.scope: Jacobi polynomial identity and positive-root preservation by finite-free multiplicative convolution, especially Proposition 2.7.
